# Hypotheses: outcome and deciding number (generated by scripts/collect_numbers.py)

- **H1** (thin rhombuses look diagonal when faint, fat ones do not): **supported**. At 10% contrast the thin rhombus is off by 33.2 deg and the fat one by 15.5 deg (at 100% contrast: 1.9 and 0.2 deg); the order holds for every lambda in a 100-fold range (tests/test_weiss.py). The fit to the digitized human data is only qualitative (RMSE 10.0 deg).
- **H2** (steady motion: a line fit beats the last echo): **supported**. RMS aim error 1.34 deg [1.30, 1.38] vs 5.75 deg [5.60, 5.89], Wilcoxon Holm p = 1.3e-81, r = -1.00, 500 trials.
- **H3** (a speed change while hidden can make prediction worse): **mixed: supported for a slow-down, not for a speed-up**. Target slowing 0.75 -> 0.19 m/s behind the occluder: error at reappearance 52.3 deg (line fit) vs 11.6 deg (last echo), Holm p = 1.3e-81; speeding up to 3 m/s: 6.5 vs 11.9 deg (prediction still better). Real bats agree for the fast change: after an occluded fast change the non-predictive model fits better (paper and here).
- **H4** (the slow prior helps only when echoes are very noisy): **supported**. The prior lowers RMS error significantly only at noise 20, 40, 80 mm (gain 2.63 deg at 80 mm, 0.010 deg at 10 mm); it never hurts significantly. On the real head-aim data the best lambda is 0 and held-out RSS is 11.73 (ours) vs 11.15 (Salles predictive): the prior does not explain the bats' head aim better.
